description_medium: The Associated Press reported on March 2, 2026, that the House committee’s Epstein investigation had questioned Bill and Hillary Clinton in depositions held the previous week. AP said the sessions veered into a leaked photo, Pizzagate, and questions about government information on UFOs. The report documents those topics, but not deliberate diversion or a link to Trump.
description_long: The Associated Press published an account on March 2, 2026, of the House committee’s investigation into Jeffrey Epstein and its depositions of former President Bill Clinton and former Secretary of State Hillary Clinton. The depositions took place the previous week. AP said the sessions veered off track, including discussion of a leaked photograph, the Pizzagate conspiracy theory, and questions about government information on UFOs. The report documents the topics it identified and characterizes the proceedings as having moved beyond the central Epstein inquiry. It does not establish how much time each subject took, whether a particular records request or investigative step was displaced, or whether Donald Trump or his allies shaped the committee’s agenda. The evidence supports a description of the depositions and the topics AP reported. It does not demonstrate the title’s causal claim that Trump-linked information chaos benefited from a deliberate turn to spectacle. A transcript and records of committee activity would be needed to assess any effect on the inquiry.
evidence_notes: Checked AP report via indexed AP result and packet. AP published the report March 2; deposition dates are Feb. 26–27. CNN link was not independently verified. No transcript or evidence of diversion/displacement found.
